brief.text: Morning. The big one is Myles Lewis-Skelly, and it's noisy rather than settled: Chelsea have actually made an enquiry (that bit is a genuine development), Sky's paper round says both Chelsea and United turned down the chance to sign him, and there's a £50m valuation floating about, so treat the whole thing as rumour-grade churn until someone bids properly. On the incoming side, a £20m wonderkid has reportedly agreed a move, which is the closest thing to real business on the board, though it's not a "here we go" yet. Elsewhere it's the usual pre-season smoke: Konsa talks still £20m short of Villa's price, ongoing chat with West Ham over a 26-year-old, Nelson possibly heading the other way, and a target who's flattered by the interest but fancies staying in Germany. Worth noting alongside all that, one squad-rule quirk means Arsenal can only make one more signing of a certain type after Bruno Guimaraes, so the shopping list may be shorter than the rumour mill suggests.

"Despite this, at 17:32 the German club confirmed that they were no longer interested due to the changed priorities in the preparation of the staff, clearly demonstrating the actual reasons underlying the failure to close the operation". clusters.title: 🚨 FA statement on Chelsea. "A financial sanction of £10 million and a suspended two-window registration ban have been imposed on Chelsea FC for breaches of The Football Association [The FA] Football Agent Regulations, Regulations on Working with Intermediaries and Third Party Investment in Players Regulations. "The FA charged Chelsea FC with 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 after its current ownership self-reported misconduct upon its purchase of the club. The FA is continuing to investigate individual misconduct arising out of this case. "Chelsea FC admitted to the 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 prior to a hearing and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-point deduction, which was to be suspended until 30 June 2027, and a £10 million fine. "The club appealed against the suspended points deduction and an independent Appeal Board allowed the appeal and set aside this sanction following a further hearing. In its place, the Appeal Board imposed a registration ban for two complete and consecutive transfer windows which is suspended until 30 June 2027. "The £10 million fine imposed by the Regulatory Commission was not subject to appeal and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football."

🚨⚠️ After medical tests done on Sunday with Napoli’s green light, Schalke 04 decide to put Jesper Lindstrøm deal on stand-by. Napoli authorized Jesper to undergo medical but Schalke are currently not proceeding after exchanging documents, as per BILD. Deal in jeopardy.

🚨🔵 Official: Napoli statement hints at possible legal action following Jesper Lindstrøm deal. “SSC Napoli reserves all actions with the competent authorities aimed at protecting their rights”. "After, yesterday, an exchange of correspondence took place on the general conditions of the contract, without ever questioning the economic terms of the agreement and the payment methods, at 13:00 today the German club informed us that some proposed clauses were not acceptable, also in light of the changed technical-sporting needs resulting from the injury of two footballers over the weekend, which would have required the modification of market strategies". "At 13:22 a response communication was sent to the German club with which, while reiterating that it was a matter of detailed changes with respect to the structure of the deal, understanding the technical needs of the German club, SSC Napoli would have been available to accept the version of the contract as proposed by Schalke". "Despite this, at 17:32 the German club confirmed that they were no longer interested due to the changed priorities in the preparation of the staff, clearly demonstrating the actual reasons underlying the failure to close the operation". "In the hope of having definitively clarified the real responsibilities for the non-transfer of the player, SSC Napoli reserves all actions with the competent authorities aimed at protecting their rights".
